entities.summary:
Delta Air Lines, Inc. is an American airline founded in 1924 as Huff Daland Dusters, a crop-dusting operation in Macon, Georgia, pivoting to passenger service in 1929 after C.E. Woolman's leadership. Today one of the world's largest airlines by revenue, Delta serves over 180 million passengers annually from its Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson hub, the world's busiest airport by passenger volume.

Delta's 2005 bankruptcy and 2008 emergence, combined with its Northwest Airlines merger, created a transformed carrier that pioneered airline ancillary revenue, SkyMiles loyalty program innovations, and corporate contract reliability. Under CEO Ed Bastian, Delta consistently ranked as the most profitable US airline and one of the most reliable for on-time performance.

Delta's Atlanta hub dominance, its Pacific routes through the former Northwest network, and its premium cabin products (Delta One, Delta Premium Select) repositioned it as the quality leader among US legacy carriers. Its investment in refinery operations (Monroe Energy) to hedge jet fuel costs was an unusual vertical integration move. Delta's response to COVID — booking middle seats empty to maintain spacing — was controversial but built significant customer loyalty. By 2023, Delta's $56 billion revenue made it one of the largest airlines in the world.
